sections.heading: 1. While you're standing
lines: ① Shift your weight from foot to foot.
② Rock gently or take a few steps.
③ One foot on a low ledge, swap every few min.
④ Bridges and side planks, 2–3 times a week.

sections.heading: 2. Stop and get checked if…
lines: Your legs tingle or feel heavy when
standing and ease when you sit down.

slides.heading: Worth getting checked if

caption:
Fine on a long walk, but your lower back aches after ten minutes in a queue? There's a reason for that.

Standing still keeps the same muscles and joints loaded without a break, so it can feel harder than walking.

Keep shifting your weight, rock gently or take a few steps when you can, and rest one foot on a low step or ledge, swapping every few minutes. Longer term, glute bridges, side planks and hip hinges build standing endurance.

Leg pain or numbness that comes on with standing and eases when you sit is worth an assessment. Our chiropractors at Hybrid Physio can look at how your back and hips are moving. Book online via the link in bio.
